rationales: Plastids mainly perform functions such as photosynthesis and storage, not aerobic respiration.
Mitochondria are the main sites of aerobic respiration in eukaryotic cells.
The nucleus stores genetic material and controls cell activities rather than carrying out aerobic respiration.
Ribosomes make proteins and are not sites of aerobic respiration.
Albumin is a protein, not the main chemical in plant cell walls.
Lignin occurs in some plant cell walls but is not their most common chemical component.
Chitin is found in fungal cell walls and arthropod exoskeletons, not commonly in plant cell walls.
Cellulose is the principal and most common chemical component of plant cell walls.
G1 is mainly a growth phase in which the cell carries out normal activities and synthesizes components.
S phase is when DNA is replicated.
M phase is when the cell divides.
During G2, the cell prepares for division, including making enzymes and other materials needed for mitosis.
Golgi is associated with the discovery of the Golgi apparatus, not meiosis.
Walther Fleming is known for describing mitosis.
Oscar Hertwig is credited with discovering meiosis.
Pasteur made major contributions to microbiology, not the discovery of meiosis.
Carbohydrates can have structural or energy roles, but enzymes are generally not carbohydrates.
Nucleic acids store and transmit genetic information; they are not the usual category of enzymes.
Lipids form membranes and store energy, but enzymes are generally not lipids.
Most enzymes are proteins that catalyze biochemical reactions.
ATP releases usable energy when a phosphate-group bond, represented here as P–P, is broken during hydrolysis.
A C–N bond is not the bond conventionally identified as the energy-releasing bond in ATP.
A C–H bond is not the bond conventionally identified as the energy-releasing bond in ATP.
A C–O bond is not the bond conventionally identified as the energy-releasing bond in ATP.
Colon bacteria do not principally produce vitamin A.
Colon bacteria do not principally produce vitamin D.
Bacteria in the colon produce vitamin K.
Vitamin C is not the vitamin chiefly produced by bacteria in the colon.
The organism level is the whole plant and is not the level described as less definite.
Tissue-level organization is present in plants and is not the intended less-definite level.
The organ-system level is less definite in plants because their organs are not grouped into clearly distinct systems as in animals.
Organs such as roots, stems, and leaves are distinguishable in plants.
An organelle is a structure within a cell, not a group of similar cells.
A tissue is a group of similar cells organized to perform the same function.
An organ consists of different tissues working together.
An organ system consists of organs working together.
Experimentation tests a hypothesis and comes after observations and reasoning.
A hypothesis is proposed to explain observations; it is not the first step.
Deduction follows from a hypothesis and is not the most basic starting step.
Taking observations is the basic starting step of the biological method.
Aristotle developed early systems for classifying organisms but did not introduce binomial nomenclature.
Robert Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification system.
Ernst Haeckel contributed to classification but did not introduce binomial nomenclature.
Carolus Linnaeus introduced the system of binomial nomenclature.
In prophase, chromosomes condense, but sister chromatids remain joined.
At metaphase, chromosomes align at the cell equator.
In anaphase, sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles.
Telophase follows chromatid separation and involves formation of new nuclei.
Metaphase I involves alignment of homologous chromosome pairs and is shorter than prophase I.
Telophase I is a brief stage following the first meiotic division.
Anaphase I is the stage when homologous chromosomes separate and is not the longest stage.
Prophase I is the longest phase of meiosis, including pairing and crossing over.
Amylase is the enzyme that breaks down starch.
Pepsin digests proteins, especially in the stomach.
Lipase digests fats.
Protease is a general term for enzymes that digest proteins, not starch.
Carbon dioxide is a reactant in photosynthesis, not its byproduct.
Oxygen is released as a byproduct of photosynthesis in the presence of sunlight.
Water is a reactant in photosynthesis, not the principal byproduct asked for.
Glucose is a product of photosynthesis, but the byproduct released is oxygen.
